short: English novelist who authored Frankenstein, pioneering the genre of science fiction.
full:
Mary Shelley was the daughter of the radical philosophers Mary Wollstonecraft and William Godwin, and she eloped with the Romantic poet Percy Bysshe Shelley at the age of sixteen. During a famously gloomy summer near Lake Geneva in 1816, she conceived the idea for her masterpiece, Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus, partly inspired by contemporary scientific debates about galvanism and the reanimation of corpses.

Published anonymously when she was just twenty, the novel was a profound cautionary tale about the ethical limits of scientific ambition and the human cost of intellectual hubris. Although she wrote numerous other works and edited her husband's poetry after his premature death, Frankenstein remains her enduring legacy, establishing the foundational tropes of science fiction and Gothic horror.
